**Runs PostgreSQL 14 – 18 · macOS and Linux** · [registry page ↗](https://doze-dev.com/registry/doze/postgres/)

<!-- recipe:start -->

Declare a Postgres server in doze.hcl, with the roles, schemas, grants and
extensions your app needs, and connect to it like any other Postgres.

doze runs the upstream PostgreSQL server, not a fork, so every client, ORM and
extension behaves as it does in production. On its first start doze creates
the database and then converges what you declared: it creates what is new,
updates what changed and drops what you removed. Your migrations own the
tables and the data.

## A database for your app

```hcl
module postgres "db" {
  version = 18
}
```

That is a whole server. Its database is named after the block (`db`), and
`doze url db` prints the line a client needs:

```sh
doze url db
# postgres://postgres@db.shop.doze:5432/db?sslmode=disable
psql "$(doze url db)"
```

The address is the block's name in your stack (`shop` here), on Postgres's own
port. See [Names and addresses](/hcl/names/) for how that works and what you
get with names off. Connecting wakes the server; it sleeps again two minutes
after the last connection closes ([Sleep and wake](/hcl/sleep/)).

To hand the URL to an app, reference it instead of copying it:

```hcl
app "api" {
  run  = "go run ./cmd/api"
  port = 8080
  env  = { DATABASE_URL = module.db.url }
}
```

The reference also orders the start: `api` waits until `db` is ready
([Start order](/hcl/start-order/)).

## One server, a role per service

Larder, the made-up grocery shop the docs use as an example, runs one Postgres
for seven services. Each service connects as its own role and owns a schema of
the same name, so the default `search_path` finds its tables and it cannot
touch anyone else's:

```hcl
module postgres "postgres" {
  version = 18
  port    = 5432

  role "catalog" { password = "catalog" }
  role "orders" { password = "orders" }

  schema "catalog" { owner = "catalog" }
  schema "orders" { owner = "orders" }
}

app "catalog" {
  run  = "go run ./services/catalog"
  port = 8002
  env = {
    DATABASE_URL = "postgres://catalog:catalog@${module.postgres.address}/postgres?sslmode=disable"
  }
}
```

`module.postgres.address` is the host and port; the URL around it says which
role to log in as.

## Roles

A role logs in unless you say `login = false`; a role that does not log in is
a group to hang grants on. A complete set: an app user, a read-only group, an
analyst in that group, and an admin:

```hcl
module postgres "shop" {
  version = 18
  owner   = "shop"

  role "shop" {
    password         = "shop"
    connection_limit = 20
  }

  role "readonly" { login = false }

  role "analyst" {
    password  = "analyst"
    member_of = ["readonly"]
  }

  role "admin" {
    password   = "admin"
    superuser  = true
    createdb   = true
    createrole = true
  }
}
```

`owner` makes a role the owner of the server's database. Every role field is
in the reference below.

## Grants

Scope a grant to a database, or to a schema, and with `objects` to every
current and future table, sequence or function in it:

```hcl
module postgres "shop" {
  version = 18
  owner   = "shop"

  role "shop" { password = "shop" }
  role "readonly" { login = false }

  grant {
    role       = "shop"
    database   = "shop"
    privileges = ["ALL"]
  }

  grant {
    role       = "readonly"
    schema     = "public"
    objects    = "tables"
    privileges = ["SELECT"]
  }
}
```

## Extensions

```hcl
module postgres "db" {
  version    = 18
  extensions = ["uuid-ossp", "pg_trgm"]

  extension "vector" { version = "0.7.0" }
  extension "hstore" { schema = "extensions" }
}
```

`extensions` is the short form; an `extension` block pins a version or a
schema. Which extensions ship with each server, and how to build one that
does not, is in [Postgres extensions](/reference/extensions/).

## Two servers side by side

Each block is its own server, with its own data, address and sleep. Two
majors run side by side:

```hcl
module postgres "db" {
  version = 18
}

module postgres "legacy" {
  version = 16
  port    = 5433
}
```

Moving a server's data to a newer major is `doze migrate`:
[Postgres major upgrades](/guides/postgres-upgrades/).

## Migrations and seed data

doze converges structure: the database, roles, schemas, grants and
extensions. Run your migrations as a [task](/hcl/tasks/), so they run before
the app that needs them, and again only when the migration files change:

```hcl
task "migrate" {
  run    = "bun x prisma migrate deploy"
  inputs = ["prisma/migrations/**/*.sql"]
  env    = { DATABASE_URL = module.db.url }
}

app "api" {
  run   = "bun run dev"
  port  = 8080
  after = [task.migrate]
  env   = { DATABASE_URL = module.db.url }
}
```

For a one-off command against a running stack, `doze run` wakes what is
declared first; `--env` puts `DATABASE_URL` and the other connection
variables in the command's environment:

```sh
doze run --env -- bin/rails db:seed
```

## Start again from nothing

```sh
doze reset db
```

`doze reset` deletes the server's data and asks first. The next connection
creates it again from doze.hcl.

## In the app

The Postgres service page has a console tab: what is running against the
database now, and which databases there are. Its overview shows the address,
what is holding it awake and when it will sleep.

## Tips

- **Dev settings by default.** `fsync` is off and `shared_buffers` is small,
  which is fast and fine for data you can recreate. Turn `fsync = true` on if
  you keep anything you would miss.
- **A pool keeps it awake.** Sleep counts connections, so a pool holding idle
  connections keeps the server up. That is usually what you want while you
  work.
- **Exact versions.** `version = 18` pins the newest 18 build in `doze.lock`;
  `version = "18.6"` asks for that build. The table below lists them.

<!-- recipe:end -->

## Reference

A real PostgreSQL server per instance — no Docker. Declare roles, schemas, extensions and grants in HCL and doze converges them: creating what's new, updating what changed, dropping what you removed. Boots on first connect, reaps when idle.

### Every field at once

<!-- ground:skip -->
```hcl
module postgres "app" {
  version          = 18
  port             = 5432
  owner            = "app"
  encoding         = "UTF8"
  locale           = "en_US.UTF-8"
  connection_limit = 50
  comment          = "primary app database"
  shared_buffers   = "256MB"
  max_connections  = 100

  settings = {
    log_min_duration_statement = "200ms"
  }

  role "app" {
    password         = "app"
    login            = true
    createdb         = true
    connection_limit = 20
    member_of        = ["readers"]
  }

  role "readers" {
    login = false
  }

  schema "analytics" {
    owner = "app"
  }

  extension "pg_trgm" {}

  grant {
    role       = "app"
    privileges = ["ALL"]
    schema     = "analytics"
    objects    = "tables"
  }
}
```

### Versions you can declare

The `version =` you write is the engine's own version. Declare a series and
doze pins its newest published build, or declare an exact build. Either way it
is fetched, verified and pinned in `doze.lock`, so it never moves on its own.

| `version =` | pins (today) | exact builds |
|---|---|---|
| `14` | `14.24.0` | 25 |
| `15` | `15.19.0` | 20 |
| `16` | `16.15.0` | 16 |
| `17` | `17.11.0` | 12 |
| `18` | `18.6.0` | 6 |

### Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | number | — | Engine major to run — 14, 15, 16, 17 or 18. **Required.** |
| `owner` | string | — | Owner role for the instance's default database. |
| `encoding` | string | `UTF8` | Character-set encoding for the database. |
| `locale` | string | — | Locale (LC_COLLATE + LC_CTYPE) for the database. |
| `lc_collate` | string | — | Collation order, overriding locale. |
| `lc_ctype` | string | — | Character classification, overriding locale. |
| `template` | string | — | Template database to create from. |
| `connection_limit` | number | `-1` | Max concurrent connections to the database. |
| `is_template` | bool | `false` | Mark the database as a template. |
| `allow_connections` | bool | `true` | Whether the database accepts connections. |
| `tablespace` | string | — | Tablespace the database lives in. |
| `comment` | string | — | COMMENT applied to the database. |
| `shared_buffers` | string | `16MB` | shared_buffers server setting, e.g. "256MB". |
| `max_connections` | number | `50` | max_connections server setting. |
| `fsync` | bool | `false` | fsync server setting (off for the dev tuning profile). |
| `autovacuum` | bool | `true` | autovacuum server setting. |
| `extensions` | list(string) | — | Shorthand list of extensions to CREATE (or use extension blocks). |
| `settings` | map(string) | — | Arbitrary postgresql.conf settings, applied verbatim. |

Every module block also takes doze's own fields: `port`, `listen`, `sleep`,
`after`, `enabled`, `routes`, `count` and `for_each`
([doze.hcl reference](/reference/doze-hcl/)).

### Nested blocks

**`role "<name>" { … }`** — A login role / user, converged on the server.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `password` | string | — | Login password. |
| `login` | bool | `true` | Whether the role may log in. |
| `superuser` | bool | `false` | Grant SUPERUSER. |
| `createdb` | bool | `false` | Allow creating databases. |
| `createrole` | bool | `false` | Allow creating other roles. |
| `replication` | bool | `false` | Allow streaming replication. |
| `inherit` | bool | `true` | Inherit privileges of member-of roles. |
| `bypassrls` | bool | `false` | Bypass row-level security. |
| `connection_limit` | number | `-1` | Per-role connection cap. |
| `valid_until` | string | — | Password expiry timestamp. |
| `member_of` | list(string) | — | Roles this role is granted membership in. |
| `comment` | string | — | COMMENT applied to the role. |
| `config` | map(string) | — | Per-role ALTER ROLE … SET settings. |

**`schema "<name>" { … }`** — A schema within the database.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | — | Role that owns the schema. |

**`extension "<name>" { … }`** — A Postgres extension to install (pgvector, postgis, …).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | string | — | Specific extension version. |
| `schema` | string | — | Schema to install the extension into. |
| `source` | string | — | Path to a local extension bundle to install from. |
| `optional` | bool | `false` | Skip (don't fail) if the extension is unavailable. |
| `cascade` | bool | `false` | CREATE EXTENSION … CASCADE for dependencies. |

**`grant { … }`** — A privilege grant to a role.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `role` | string | — | The role the privileges go to. **Required.** |
| `privileges` | list(string) | — | Privileges to grant (SELECT, INSERT, ALL, …). **Required.** |
| `database` | string | — | Target database. |
| `schema` | string | — | Target schema. |
| `objects` | string | — | Object class the grant applies to (tables, sequences, …). |
| `with_grant_option` | bool | `false` | Allow the grantee to re-grant. |

### Module releases

The releases of the module that provide this engine. doze picks the newest
one that fits your doze and your `version =`, and pins it in `doze.lock`;
you never write these. Older releases stay available for pinned lockfiles.
